clue.text: Wise as inept characters may become

indicators.note: the letters (characters) of the words before are what can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: An ironic remark that wisdom is what foolish people can turn into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters may become' asks you to rearrange the letters of AS INEPT; 'inept' looks like the opposite of the definition, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal synonym for wise or discerning.

clue.text: Quiet girl on an Irish river

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A silent young woman beside a river in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.

clue.text: A young farmer may have his share

definitions.text: A young farmer may have his share

parts.words: A young farmer may have his share
parts.note: share reads as a portion, but here is the ploughshare, the blade a young farm hand guides

explanation.definitionFit: A ploughboy was a lad who led or drove the plough team.

clue.text: Resin of help to ukulele minstrels

indicators.note: the answer is found within, giving help to the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tree gum useful to ukulele players.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across ukulELE MInstrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant gum from tropical trees, used in varnishes.

clue.text: Conversation above board? No, under and around it

definitions.text: Conversation above board? No, under and around it

parts.words: Conversation above board? No, under and around it
parts.note: above board means honest, but here the board is a dining table, with chat over it

explanation.definitionFit: Table talk is informal conversation at meals.

clue.text: Two girls quietly returning to a royal burial-place

indicators.note: returning means the girls' names and the quiet sign are read backwards, the whole run turned

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
Mary is a girl's name
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Two young women tiptoe back to visit a royal tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole string DIMARYP backwards; 'to' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pharaohs were entombed in pyramids, so one is a monarch's tomb.

clue.text: Guide whose fall was drawn by Tenniel

definitions.text: whose fall was drawn by Tenniel

explanation.surface: A guide whose downfall was illustrated by a famous artist.
explanation.walkthrough: John Tenniel's 1890 Punch cartoon 'Dropping the Pilot' showed Bismarck leaving the ship of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot steers ships into port, and Tenniel's cartoon shows a pilot being dropped.

clue.text: Soldiers raising objections' but proving to be wrong

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
butting means pushing against or opposing

explanation.surface: Troops protest yet turn out to be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut a claim is to disprove it, showing it is false.

clue.text: Low quarters for a debarker

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
S and E, south and east, are compass quarters

explanation.surface: Cattle stalls given to a tree-stripping animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Moose strip bark from trees, so a debarker; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moose gnaw and strip tree bark in winter.

clue.text: A course to abandon, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the abandoning word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: to desert means to abandon

explanation.surface: A meal stage you might want to skip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course at the end of a meal.

clue.text: About to open the beer by oneself

indicators.note: the 'about' word is set inside, opening up the beer word

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Opening a beer when drinking solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to open' places ON (about, as in 'a book on birds') inside ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alone is to be on your own, without company.

clue.text: They indicate a course for hotel attendants, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the attendants' word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: bellboys carry luggage in hotels

explanation.surface: Hotel staff seem to be showing guests the way to a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals that BELLBOYS sounds like the answer; 'course' is a sea route, not a meal or a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell buoys are floating markers that ring to show ships a safe channel.

clue.text: Not caring for books on informal wear

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the books come after, set on the end of the clothing

parts.note: a negligé is a light, loose dressing gown
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes reading about casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: NEGLIGE is the unaccented spelling of negligée; 'on' puts NT after it. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent describes someone careless, failing to take proper care.

clue.text: Subject for this kind of song

explanation.surface: A topic suitable for a certain sort of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic of a work, and a theme song is the signature tune of a show or film.

clue.text: Apprehend the old boy — he's rich and powerful

parts.note: to nab is to arrest or catch
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Police arrest an elderly man who turns out to be a wealthy grandee.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was originally a Mughal governor, later any very wealthy, influential person.

clue.text: Supporter I brought down 'a couple of steps to this bar

indicators.note: the named letter shifts two places further down the word

parts.note: a brassiere is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A lingerie item carried down a short flight to a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In BRASSIERE, the I moves two places later to make the answer; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal restaurant serving drinks, a bar-café.

clue.text: This vicar is eccentric as a keeper of records

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: An odd clergyman doubles as the parish record-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is eccentric' rearranges THIS VICAR; 'as' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist looks after historical documents and records.

clue.text: It makes liquor available for an Irish prison warder

explanation.surface: A tool that opens bottles, or a jailer from a Munster city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is an Irish city and 'screw' is British slang for a prison officer.
explanation.definitionFit: This tool draws corks from wine bottles, and a 'screw' from Cork would be an Irish guard.

clue.text: One may be spotted alone in this

definitions.text: One may be spotted alone in this

parts.words: One may be spotted alone in this
parts.note: spotted means noticed, but also covered in spots, as a measles patient kept apart

explanation.definitionFit: Patients with infectious diseases are quarantined in a separate ward.

clue.text: Two birds taking a chance on the way?

definitions.text: Two birds taking a chance on the way?

parts.words: Two birds taking a chance on the way?
parts.note: a jay is a bird, and a strolling bird is a walker; together they picture a pedestrian risking the road

explanation.definitionFit: A jaywalker crosses the street carelessly, ignoring traffic signals.

clue.text: There's a case for putting him in a box

definitions.text: There's a case for putting him in a box

parts.words: There's a case for putting him in a box
parts.note: a case is a trial, and the box is where jurors sit in court

explanation.definitionFit: A juror sits in the jury box to hear a trial.

clue.text: Rise about right for pop musicians

indicators.note: about means the rising phrase goes round the right letter

parts.note: to go up is to rise

explanation.surface: A climb in the charts sounds right for some pop stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps GO UP around R; 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a band of performers, such as a rock or pop group.

clue.text: Page allowed to eat a president's cake

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the president goes inside

parts.note: let means allowed
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A page boy is permitted a presidential slice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts IKE inside P + LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a thin crumpet or small pancake, a teatime cake in Britain.

clue.text: Lawrence by another name kept Oriental flowers

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the Oriental letter sits within the alias

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross
E stands for East, hence oriental

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia, under an alias, grew some Eastern blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) served as Aircraftman Ross; 'kept' places E inside ROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses are among the best known garden blooms.

clue.text: Quick gain from this exclusive story?

explanation.surface: A fast profit from a newspaper exclusive.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is a quick big profit, and also a news story one paper gets first.

clue.text: Pithy remark by 1 ac is first-class

parts.note: 1 across is SAPIENT, which means wise
crack as an adjective means expert or top-rate, as in a crack shot

explanation.surface: A neat quip from a clever person rated excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' refers to the answer at 1 across, meaning wise; 'by' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, witty comment or quip.

clue.text: Revives a northern holiday

explanation.surface: Brings something back with a northern break.
explanation.walkthrough: Wakes Weeks were annual mill-town holidays in Lancashire and northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wakes means rouses, and the Wakes are traditional holidays in northern English towns.

clue.text: Two firms meet over a drink

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the firms sit above the final letter

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a second Co, another company

explanation.surface: Two companies merge over a beverage deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage.

clue.text: Sail for ark, no more in, need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Noah's vessel needs mending before it can carry any more sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of repair' rearranges ARK NO MORE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonraker is a small sail set above the skysail on a square-rigger.

clue.text: Complaint made when the relish: is left unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the relish word is dropped

parts.note: chilli is a hot sauce or relish

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles when the sauce runs out before the meal ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left unfinished' removes the last letter of CHILLI. 'Complaint' is an ailment, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a minor illness, a cold, and a complaint can mean an ailment.

clue.text: What little jaws these kids have!

definitions.text: What little jaws these kids have!

parts.words: What little jaws these kids have!
parts.note: pincers or claws that nip are one sense, and small children are another

explanation.definitionFit: Nippers are claws or pincers, and in British slang nippers are small children.

clue.text: A portable stand or something

explanation.surface: Looking for a movable stand or any item at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a light stand of open shelves, and also a vague term for an unnamed thing.
